intro: Chonburi is just over an hour's drive from Bangkok but packs the sea, temples, gardens, night markets, and cliffside cafés all into one province. We've gathered 10 places that people talk about most after visiting — from Pattaya and Bang Saen to Koh Si Chang. Pick the ones that suit you and start planning.
chips: 🏯 Cliffside wooden temple by the sea
🦛 Moo Deng at Khao Kheow Zoo
🛶 Koh Si Chang, the white bridge

blocks.html:
The charm of Chonburi is how much you can do within a short distance. On the Pattaya side you have Terminal 21 — the airport-themed mall where each floor recreates a different world city — the Thepprasit Night Market with its long run of street food stalls, and The Sky Gallery cliffside café with sea views. Drive south toward Sattahip and you hit Nong Nooch Garden and Khao Chi Chan. For real Thai beach vibes there's Bang Saen, where you rent a beach chair, order fresh seafood, and spend the day listening to the waves — or take the ferry from Si Racha pier across to Koh Si Chang and walk the white Atsadang Bridge stretching out to sea. One trip gets you the sea, culture, and photo spots all at once.

Several places on this list have a landmark quality that goes well beyond Chonburi. The Sanctuary of Truth in Naklua is an entirely hand-carved wooden palace by the sea, nearly 100 meters tall, and still under construction after several decades. Khao Chi Chan has the largest cliff-engraved Buddha image in Thailand. Khao Kheow Open Zoo in Si Racha is now famous worldwide because of Moo Deng, the viral pygmy hippo drawing visitors from across the globe. Each place has a distinct identity. Read through, choose where you want to go first.

blocks.name: Sanctuary of Truth
blocks.area: Naklua, North Pattaya, Bang Lamung District, Chonburi
blocks.signature: Entirely hand-carved teak palace by the sea, nearly 100 meters tall, still under construction after several decades
blocks.descHtml:
The Sanctuary of Truth is a fully hand-carved wooden palace on the cape at Rachavej, Naklua, Pattaya. The structure stands about 105 meters tall, built entirely from teak and hardwood with not a single iron nail used. The detail that strikes most visitors is that it isn't finished — craftsmen are visibly at work carving, and they have been for decades. You get both the finished grandeur and the living process at the same time. Well suited to people who love art and architecture, photography, and families who want to show children something genuinely rare.

What you can't miss is the carved wood across all four wings, each reflecting a different artistic tradition — Thai, Khmer, Chinese, and Indian. The detail is dense enough that you need to walk slowly to take it in. Entry requires wearing a hard hat because construction is ongoing. Multiple reviews say the evening round has the best atmosphere — the sea breeze is cool, the light is good for photography, and the daytime heat has passed. The site also runs boat shows and cultural performances on a schedule. Activities like elephant or horse riding are mentioned in some reviews with welfare concerns — skip them if you'd rather not.

Adult entry: 500 THB for daytime, 700 THB for the evening round. Children 110–140 cm pay 250/350 THB; under 110 cm free. Open daily — daytime round approximately 08:20–18:00, evening round 18:20–20:30. Located about 3 km from central Pattaya. Online pre-booking sometimes gives a small discount.

This place ranks high because there is nothing else like it — a hand-carved wooden sea-cliff palace at no point claiming to be done. Reviews consistently praise the craftsmanship, the cleanliness, and the organization. The crowd peaks in high season. Dress respectfully, wear the hard hat as instructed, budget about 1–2 hours to walk the grounds at a proper pace.
mustOrder: Four carved wings — Thai, Khmer, Chinese, Indian traditions
105-meter wooden palace right on the sea
Boat shows and cultural performances
Photography spots along Cape Rachavej
blocks.bestFor: Evening visit for sea views and photography

blocks.name: Nong Nooch Tropical Garden Pattaya
blocks.area: Na Chom Thian, Sattahip District, Chonburi
blocks.signature: Vast botanical park with a French formal garden, life-size dinosaur valley, elephant show, and Thai cultural performance
blocks.descHtml:
Nong Nooch Tropical Garden Pattaya is an enormous tropical botanical garden over 1,700 rai that takes the idea of a garden visit to a completely different level — because inside there isn't just plants. There are fully themed garden zones: a French-style garden with geometrically clipped hedges stretching as far as the eye can see, a Stonehenge replica, a cactus garden, and a Dinosaur Valley with hundreds of life-size dinosaur models where children can run around and take photos. Perfect for families, photography-focused couples, and anyone who wants a full day out without getting bored.

The highlights most visitors talk about are two major shows running multiple times a day: a Thai cultural performance in the main theater, and an elephant show involving football, painting, and ring-tossing that draws applause from the crowd. Reviews broadly praise how well-maintained the garden is, how beautifully landscaped, and how you can walk and shoot photos for hours without running out of things to frame. Most people recommend budgeting at least half a day — the grounds are genuinely large. Some zones require a tram or cart to cover.

Budget-friendly: a basic entry ticket starts in the hundreds of baht; a package including the garden plus both the cultural show and elephant show is around 400 THB for an adult — good value for a full day. Located in Na Chom Thian, Sattahip, about 15 km from central Pattaya. Open daily 08:00–18:00. Come in the morning when it's cooler, the light is better, and you have the whole day ahead.

This place has consistently ranked near the top in Pattaya because it puts everything in one place: beautiful gardens, entertaining shows, photography spots, food, and shopping. Wear comfortable walking shoes and carry water — there's a lot of ground to cover and it can be sunny. For those with animal welfare concerns, the cultural show can be enjoyed without the elephant show.
mustOrder: French formal garden and Stonehenge replica
Dinosaur Valley with life-size models
Elephant show
Thai cultural performance

blocks.name: Terminal 21 Pattaya
blocks.signature: Airport-themed mall where each floor recreates a famous world city — London, Tokyo, Paris, San Francisco — with a real aircraft parked out front as the check-in photo spot
blocks.descHtml:
If you're picking one mall in Pattaya to walk around and take photos, Terminal 21 Pattaya is the first name that comes up. The concept is an airport terminal where each floor recreates a different world city — London, Tokyo, Paris, San Francisco, Italy. The instant identifier is the full-size commercial aircraft parked outside the entrance, which has become the check-in photo spot that almost every visitor stops at. Great for families, couples, or photography-minded visitors who want interesting frames without paying entry.

Inside, each floor genuinely looks different. London has a red double-decker bus. Paris has a scaled Eiffel Tower. Tokyo has a charming Japanese aesthetic. Even the bathrooms are decorated to the floor's theme — multiple reviews single them out as some of the nicest in Pattaya. Other highlights include the long escalator that has become a landmark in its own right, and the food court upstairs with a wide range of affordable options — from Thai street dishes to international food — all at prices well below the sit-down restaurants elsewhere in the mall.

No entry fee — browse as much or as little as you like. The food court is the main spending zone; sit-down restaurants inside run higher. Located on Second Road (Pattaya Sai Song) near North Pattaya — easy to reach, close to the beach. Open daily 11:00–22:00, Friday to Sunday until 23:00. Wide corridors, stroller and wheelchair accessible. There's an SF cinema, a supermarket, and a kids' zone.

Google rating at 4.6 from over 29,000 reviews reflects genuine visitor satisfaction. The peak crowd time is evenings and public holidays — if you want the aircraft photo without too many people in frame, come mid-morning or early afternoon.
mustOrder: Real aircraft outside — the check-in photo spot
Each-floor world-city themes — London, Tokyo, Paris
Landmark escalator
Food court — wide variety at low prices

blocks.name: Koh Si Chang (Atsadang Bridge · Phra Chudadhuj Royal Palace)
blocks.signature: White wooden Atsadang Bridge stretching out to sea, paired with the Phra Chudadhuj Royal Palace from the reign of Rama V — the only island in Thailand that served as a royal residence
blocks.descHtml:
If you want to get out on the water without a long drive, Koh Si Chang is the answer. Take the ferry from Ko Loi Pier in Si Racha — about 45 minutes — and you land on an island with genuine historical depth. The highlight everyone comes for is the Atsadang Bridge: a white wooden pier extending straight out to sea within the Phra Chudadhuj Royal Palace grounds. The white of the bridge against the sky and sea is what makes it the island's most-photographed spot. Well suited to café-hopping visitors, couples, and anyone who wants a relaxed day trip.

The site is special because it's the only royal palace on an island in Thailand, used as a royal residence during the reign of Rama V from 1892. Within the palace grounds are several old wooden pavilions to explore — Wattana House, Phong Sri House, Apirom House — plus a white chedi on a small hill, a stream, large trees, and benches spaced along the paths. Reviews consistently describe the atmosphere as quiet and easy, and recommend budgeting 2–3 hours to walk at a comfortable pace.

Very budget-friendly: entry to the palace and the Atsadang Bridge is free. The main cost is the ferry and the island sky lab (a small shared pickup truck) that shuttles visitors to different points around the island. The museum opens approximately 09:00–17:00, closed Mondays (sometimes Tuesdays too — check before going). Dress modestly — a T-shirt and shorts are fine but swimwear is not permitted inside the palace grounds.

Popular because it combines the sea, history, and beautiful photography in one place, and it's close to Bangkok. For the best clean shot of the bridge, come in the early morning or late afternoon — the light is softer and fewer people are walking across.
mustOrder: Atsadang Bridge (white wooden pier stretching out to sea)
Phra Chudadhuj Royal Palace — Thailand's only island royal residence
White chedi on the small hill
Old wooden pavilions from the Rama V era
blocks.bestFor: Day trip, white-bridge photography, couples and friend groups
blocks.zone: Koh Si Chang (ferry from Si Racha)

blocks.name: Bang Saen Beach · Khao Sam Muk Viewpoint
blocks.area: Saen Suk, Mueang Chonburi District, Chonburi
blocks.signature: The Thai locals' own beach — rent a beach chair, eat fresh seafood by the water — paired with Khao Sam Muk viewpoint for a wide bay view, a Chinese shrine, and wild monkeys
blocks.priceRange: Free entry · beach chairs a few dozen THB · food 100–250 THB/person
blocks.descHtml:
Bang Saen is the genuinely local beach in Chonburi, just over an hour from Bangkok. The appeal here is renting a beach chair and umbrella by the sand, ordering fresh seafood — blue crab som tam, oysters, whatever is fresh — and spending the day reclining to the sound of the waves. Well suited to families, groups of friends, and anyone who wants the sea nearby without overplanning. Arrive, get in the water, rent a rubber ring, hire a horse for a shoreline ride, or just cycle along the beach path.

Paired with the beach is Khao Sam Muk viewpoint — a short drive up a gentle hill, a few minutes by car, and you reach a spot that overlooks the entire Bang Saen Bay in one wide sweep. It's a popular photography viewpoint that has recently been improved. Nearby is the Sam Muk Chinese Shrine, an old Chinese temple under a cliff face that locals visit regularly to make offerings. And the hill's other famous occupants are the wild monkeys who have lived there for generations, wandering freely and approaching anyone carrying food.

Very affordable: beach chair rental costs a few dozen baht per chair, good for the whole day. Seafood per person runs around 100–250 THB. Khao Sam Muk viewpoint and the shrine are free to enter. There are parking areas and food stalls nearby. The beach and water are accessible all day; the shrine and shops along the beach run approximately 06:00–18:00. Mondays are a beach-cleaning day — most beach chairs, umbrellas, and shoreline stalls don't operate. If you're specifically coming for beach chairs and seafood, avoid Mondays. During long public holidays, it gets very busy — arrive early to claim a waterfront spot.

Key tip: the monkeys on Khao Sam Muk are semi-wild and opportunistic. Don't carry visible food bags, keep your glasses, phone, and valuables secured, and close car windows. On the beach side, Google rating for the Khao Sam Muk viewpoint runs at around 4.4 from over a thousand reviews, reflecting genuinely high satisfaction with the views.
mustOrder: Beach chair, seafood lunch by the sea
Khao Sam Muk viewpoint over Bang Saen Bay
Sam Muk Chinese Shrine
Watch the wild monkey troop on the hill
blocks.bestFor: Midday lunch by the sea, family and friend groups, watching the sunset
blocks.hours: Beach open all day · shrine/shops 06:00–18:00 (no beach chairs on Mondays)

blocks.title: 🛏️ Where to Stay in Chonburi–Pattaya
blocks.text: Picking the right base in Chonburi makes a real difference depending on your trip. Want to walk to shops and eat conveniently? North Pattaya near Terminal 21 is the call. Want to wake up facing the water? Look at Jomtien Beach or Phra Tamnak. Prefer a relaxed family atmosphere? The Bang Saen–Si Racha zone is close to Khao Kheow Zoo. Options run from hostels to beachfront resorts. Compare prices and check availability before booking.

blocks.name: Khao Chi Chan
blocks.area: Na Chom Thian, Sattahip District, Chonburi
blocks.signature: Laser-engraved Buddha image inlaid with gold mosaic on a natural cliff face — approximately 109 x 70 meters — the largest cliff-engraved Buddha in Thailand
blocks.descHtml:
Khao Chi Chan is a distinctive limestone hill in the middle of the flatlands of Na Chom Thian, Sattahip, and has become the defining landmark of Chonburi province. What everyone comes to see is Phra Phuttha Maha Wachira Uttamo Phasa Sada — a Maravijaya-posture Buddha image engraved into the cliff face using laser etching and inlaid with gold mosaic tiles, measuring approximately 109 x 70 meters. It's the largest cliff-engraved Buddha in Thailand, created in 1996 to mark the 50th anniversary of King Rama IX's accession to the throne. Good for visitors who want to pay respects, photography enthusiasts who want a dramatic landscape shot, and anyone looking for a peaceful stop close to Pattaya without crowds.

The highlight you can't miss is standing on the open plaza at the base and looking up at the golden Buddha set against the grey limestone cliff face. The image looks best when morning or late-afternoon sun hits the cliff directly — the gold tiles catch the light at their brightest. The surrounding grounds are landscaped and wide, with a reflection pool that mirrors the image and, in some seasons, flowering gardens extending the frame. Reviews consistently describe the atmosphere as spacious and awe-inspiring, with plenty of room to walk around for an hour at a relaxed pace.

Free entry. No admission charge, just a donation box. The car park is wide and accommodates both private cars and tour buses. Open daily approximately 06:00–18:00. Located along Highway 331, easy to reach by car from Pattaya or Na Chom Thian. Works naturally as a pairing with Nong Nooch Garden or a nearby beach in a single trip. The whole day costs almost nothing beyond fuel and any food from the small stalls near the entrance.

Popular because it's simultaneously a sacred site and a photography landmark that produces genuinely dramatic images in a single visit. Free, easy to reach, not much walking required. The open plaza gets strong midday sun — bring a hat, apply sunscreen, and avoid arriving at noon. In overcast or rainy weather, clouds may partially obscure the image. Dress modestly as this is a place of worship.
mustOrder: Gold-inlaid cliff Buddha, 109 x 70 m — view from the plaza below
Reflection pool photo of the Buddha
Wide garden grounds surrounding the hill
blocks.bestFor: Morning or evening visit for worship and dramatic cliff photography

blocks.name: Pattaya Floating Market (Four Regions)
blocks.area: Nong Prue, Bang Lamung District, Pattaya
blocks.signature: Recreated Thai village houses from all four regions of the country, canal boat rides, regional food, a 20-THB souvenir zone, and Thai cultural performances
blocks.descHtml:
Pattaya Floating Market (Four Regions) is a large recreated floating market that brings the style of Thai village architecture from all four regions — North, Central, Northeast, and South — together on a 70-rai site along Sukhumvit Road. Walking from the Central-style wooden houses to the Southern-style pavilions is like touring all of Thailand in one afternoon. Well suited to families with mixed ages, visitors who want a relaxing walkthrough, photography enthusiasts who want Thai waterside architecture, and international visitors who want a compact introduction to Thai regional life.

The highlight many visitors mention is the boat ride around the market canal — wooden paddle boats and some amphibious options, at around 150 THB per ride. Another popular zone is the 20-THB souvenir shop where you can pick up small gifts and trinkets at a flat price without bargaining. Food runs the full regional spread: traditional ice cream, boat noodles, grilled squid, khao lam (bamboo-tube sticky rice), durian sticky rice — and unusual options like grilled crocodile for adventurous eaters. Throughout the day the site runs free Thai cultural shows including ram Thai dancing and Muay Thai on the water, weaving demonstrations, a love bridge, and a zip-line across the canal.

Open daily approximately 10:00–20:00. Thai nationals enter free; foreigners pay approximately 200 THB. Located on the south Pattaya side toward Sattahip, about 2–3 km from South Pattaya. Easy by car or taxi. Google rating at 3.9 from tens of thousands of reviews reflects that most visitors enjoy it but have realistic expectations. The place is more of a tourist recreation than a traditional floating market — some reviewers note that vendors can be repetitive and the boat rides sometimes pass limited shoreside stalls. If you come expecting to walk around, eat your way through regional food, and watch a show, you'll get your money's worth in about 1.5–2 hours.

Practical tips: bring cash in small notes as many stalls are cash-only. The outdoor walkways can be very hot at midday — come in the late afternoon or evening for better comfort and to catch the cultural performances. Groups eating together can split food from multiple stalls and share the table, which is the most cost-effective way to try variety.
mustOrder: Canal boat ride (~150 THB)
20-THB souvenir zone
Regional waterside food — khao lam, durian sticky rice
Thai cultural show and Muay Thai on the water
blocks.bestFor: Families and groups, browsing and eating in the late afternoon to evening

blocks.name: Thepprasit Night Market
blocks.area: Mueang Pattaya, Bang Lamung District, Chonburi
blocks.signature: Pattaya's largest and liveliest night market, with a clear food zone and shopping zone, extensive street food, and organized stall rows under a covered walkway
blocks.descHtml:
If you're looking for one night market that genuinely represents Pattaya, Thepprasit Night Market is the answer. It's the biggest and most active night market in the city, open since 1999, with several hundred stalls total. The layout is well organized: one side is street food running in a long straight line; the other side is clothing, shoes, bags, home goods, jewelry, nail bars, lash extensions, and even a pet café. Good for anyone who wants to eat and shop in one place — families, friend groups, and international visitors who want a real Thai market rather than a tourist showpiece.

The food is the main event. Every region of Thailand is represented: grilled skewers and pork, salt-crust grilled fish, fresh seafood — grilled prawns, squid — spicy salads, noodle soup, and unusual options like fried insects and scorpions for those who want to try something outside the usual. Desserts include honey mango with fish sauce, lychee shaved ice, and more. Multiple reviews agree: generous portions, fair prices, and the desserts in particular get high praise. The food zone has shared seating at the front — order from whichever stall you like and bring everything to one table.

Free entry. One meal runs around 60–120 THB per person; seafood dishes run 150–250 THB; snacks and desserts 30–80 THB. Many reviewers note that prices here haven't been inflated for tourists the way other Pattaya spots have, because locals genuinely use this market. Located on Thepprasit Road, South Pattaya, near the Sukhumvit junction and an outlet mall. Large parking area, free bathrooms. Open daily approximately 17:00–23:00, but Fridays through Sundays are when the full market is open and the energy is best.

Popular because it packs everything a market visitor wants into one well-organized place: clean, orderly walkways, a covered area for comfort, and genuine value. Bring small banknotes — many stalls don't take cards. Arriving around 19:00 is when the market hits its stride and all the stalls are open.
mustOrder: Fresh seafood — grilled prawns, grilled squid
Salt-crust grilled fish / grilled pork skewers
Mango with sweet fish sauce / shaved ice
Fried insects — adventurous optional
blocks.bestFor: Evening dinner and shopping, groups and families

blocks.name: Khao Kheow Open Zoo
blocks.signature: Massive open zoo over 5,000 rai with 8,000+ animals across 300+ species — the star is Moo Deng, the viral pygmy hippo
blocks.descHtml:
Khao Kheow Open Zoo is a massive open-format zoo across more than 5,000 rai in Bang Phra subdistrict, Si Racha, Chonburi. Animals are kept in habitat-style enclosures with more space than typical caged settings. It houses over 8,000 animals from more than 300 species, making it one of the largest zoos in Asia. Well suited to families bringing children, animal lovers, and anyone who wants a day in a forested setting within easy distance of Bangkok or Pattaya — about 1.5 to 2 hours' drive from the capital.

The current star who made the zoo globally famous is Moo Deng — a pygmy hippo calf who went viral in 2024 and has had visitors queuing for the hippo enclosure ever since. Beyond Moo Deng there are plenty of other zones worth visiting: giraffe feeding, hippopotamus, zebra, tigers, a penguin area, and in some periods a Khao Kheow Night Safari after dark. Real reviews consistently say the grounds are very large — renting a golf cart or bringing your own car into the zone is much more comfortable than walking the whole thing in the heat.

Entry is approximately 200 THB per adult. Children under a certain height, senior citizens over 60, and those with disabilities may enter at a discount or free depending on current policy. Car admission is around an extra 80 THB. The entry fee covers all animal zones including the Moo Deng hippo enclosure at no extra charge. Open daily 08:00–17:00. Experienced visitors recommend arriving at opening (08:00) or around 14:00 to see Moo Deng when she's active — avoid midday when she tends to sleep from the heat, and avoid weekends in peak season if possible.

Popular because it packages natural open-habitat zoo experience, wide green grounds, and the Moo Deng draw in one place. Key tips: it gets genuinely hot and there are insects — bring a hat, water, sunscreen, and mosquito spray. Wear shoes you can walk long distances in. Budget the full day if you want to see everything properly. On holidays, parking fills up early.
mustOrder: Moo Deng — viral pygmy hippo
Giraffe and hippo feeding
Golf cart tour through open animal zones
Penguin area and tiger zone
blocks.bestFor: Family day out / seeing Moo Deng

blocks.name: The Sky Gallery Pattaya
blocks.signature: Cliffside café-restaurant with 180° sea views, multiple seating zones, and famous for sunset hour — with cocktails and honey toast
blocks.descHtml:
The Sky Gallery Pattaya is a café and restaurant perched on the Phra Tamnak Hill cliff face — one of those places Pattaya visitors regularly get invited to visit. The main draw is a wide open sea view stretching nearly 180 degrees, taking in Pattaya Bay and Koh Larn in the distance, especially as the sky shifts colour around sunset. Well suited to couples, photography enthusiasts, and groups of friends who want to sit back with a sea breeze without actually going down to the beach. The restaurant sits in front of the Cosy Beach Hotel on Phra Tamnak Road — you park and walk a short distance down, but once the view opens up most people say it's worth it.

Seating is spread across several distinct zones: cliff-edge tables with the best views, soft sofa areas, an outdoor sand section for photos, shaded garden seating, and an air-conditioned indoor zone for those who want to escape the sun. The menu is international and Thai: pizza, pasta, risotto alongside tom yum goong, som tam, and fresh seafood. Desserts include a signature honey toast. The drinks list covers cocktails, mocktails, and coffee. Reviews generally rate the view and atmosphere as the main attraction, with the food at a solid but not exceptional level — good enough to enjoy alongside the scenery.

No entry fee — just order food or drinks normally. Budget around 300–700 THB per person depending on how much you order. Open daily from mid-morning until late; the peak window is around 17:00–18:30 when everyone arrives to watch the sunset. Arrive before that window or book a cliff-edge table in advance if you want the best spot. On weekends the terrace fills up fast and parking is limited — arrive early to avoid the scramble. The evening view of the lit bay is also worth staying for.
mustOrder: Cliff-edge table at sunset — best view of the bay
Honey toast
Pizza / risotto
Cocktail with the sea breeze
blocks.bestFor: Watching the sunset over the sea with a partner or group

blocks.title: What to know before visiting Chonburi

items.title: Getting around
items.text: From Bangkok it is about a 90-minute drive to Pattaya. Within town, use the Grab app or hop on the blue songthaew (shared pickup trucks). For Koh Sichang you drive to Si Racha pier, then take a passenger ferry across.

items.title: Carry cash
items.text: Street food markets like Thepprasit and beach vendors at Bang Saen mostly take cash, so carry small Thai baht notes. Malls, big attractions, and cafes such as The Sky Gallery accept cards and QR payment.

items.title: Timing — skip the queues
items.text: Visit outdoor spots like Sanctuary of Truth, Nong Nooch, and Khao Kheow Zoo in the morning to dodge the heat and crowds. To meet Moo Deng the pygmy hippo when she is active, arrive before noon.

items.title: Tipping
items.text: Tipping is not required but appreciated. Rounding up the bill at restaurants or leaving small change for songthaew drivers and the staff who carry your beach chairs is a kind gesture.

items.title: Language — English menus
items.text: Pattaya is very tourist-friendly with English menus and signs almost everywhere. At local Bang Saen seafood stalls English may be limited, but pointing at the fish or photos works just fine.

items.title: Foreigner pricing
items.text: Some attractions have separate pricing for foreigners (for example Pattaya Floating Market). Booking entry tickets online in advance via Klook or GetYourGuide can save time and sometimes money.

blocks.title: Plan your Chonburi trip to make it count
blocks.html:
If you have two days, split by zone. Day one covers Pattaya and Sattahip: start the morning at Nong Nooch Garden since the elephant and cultural shows run multiple times and you want the full experience — Khao Chi Chan is nearby and makes a natural second stop. In the late afternoon head to The Sky Gallery for the sunset, then end the night at Thepprasit Night Market, which is Pattaya's most lively evening option.

Day two: get to the Sanctuary of Truth in the morning when the sun is not yet at its strongest — or if you want the atmosphere and the light effects, book the evening round. Then drive north to Bang Saen or take the ferry from Si Racha across to Koh Si Chang. For Khao Kheow Open Zoo, arriving before noon is important if you want to see Moo Deng when she is most active — the heat in the afternoon tends to make her sleep.

blocks.text: Enjoying Chonburi properly means picking the right base. Whether you want to be within walking distance of Terminal 21 in North Pattaya, wake up facing Jomtien Beach, or stay quietly near Bang Saen, there are good options at every budget — check availability now.

faq.q: Which Chonburi attractions should you not miss?
faq.a: For a first visit, the two places people mention most are the Sanctuary of Truth in Naklua — a hand-carved wooden sea palace standing nearly 100 meters tall — and Khao Kheow Open Zoo in Si Racha, now famous worldwide for Moo Deng the viral pygmy hippo. These two get the most attention in Chonburi right now.

faq.q: What are the highlights of Chonburi?
faq.a: Chonburi covers a lot of ground. Landmark attractions include the Sanctuary of Truth and Khao Chi Chan, which has the largest cliff-engraved Buddha in Thailand. For nature there's Nong Nooch Garden and Bang Saen Beach. For island and sea day trips there's Koh Si Chang. For shopping and food there's Terminal 21 and Thepprasit Night Market. Sea, culture, and food — all in one province.

faq.q: Are entry fees expensive for Chonburi attractions?
faq.a: Several places are free: Terminal 21, Khao Chi Chan, Bang Saen Beach, and The Sky Gallery (you pay for food only). Paid attractions include the Sanctuary of Truth at around 500 THB daytime and 700 THB evening; Nong Nooch Garden at around 150–400 THB; and Khao Kheow Open Zoo at around 200 THB. Children and senior citizens usually get discounts. Pattaya Floating Market is free for Thai nationals; foreigners pay around 200 THB.

faq.q: How do you get around Chonburi and is parking easy?
faq.a: It's about a 90-minute drive from Bangkok to Pattaya. Most attractions have their own parking areas. Within central Pattaya you can use Grab or hop on the blue songthaew shared pickup trucks. For Koh Si Chang you drive to Si Racha pier and take the ferry across — on the island, sky lab shared tuk-tuks shuttle visitors between points.

Outdoor attractions like the Sanctuary of Truth, Nong Nooch Garden, and Khao Kheow Open Zoo open in the morning — go early to avoid the heat and crowds. Terminal 21 opens like a standard mall and runs until late. Thepprasit Night Market starts in the early evening and is fullest on Fridays through Sundays. The Sky Gallery is busiest in the late afternoon for the sunset. Check each venue's latest hours before you go.
